papers.relied_on: Row 32 D7 used the 2000-2014 DKA hospitalization trend as context for the size of the DKA population (excerpt only).
papers.full_text_shows: NIS 2014 estimate of 188,950 DKA hospitalizations (first-listed ICD-9-CM 250.1, all ages, all diabetes types), rate 30.2 per 1,000 persons with diabetes, up 54.9% from 2009. Diabetes type was not available, so the paper gives no count of DKA in people not coded type 1; it says DKA is more frequent in established than new disease but that this is unknown in adults.
papers.quote: Because diabetes type was not collected in NHIS, rates were not stratified by disease type.
papers.key_numbers: 2014: 188,950 DKA hospitalizations; 30.2 per 1,000 (95% CI 26.4-34.0); 2009 to 2014 +54.9%; in-hospital case fatality 1.1% to 0.4%
papers.role_in_work: Background magnitude of DKA events for the D7 count of row 32; not used for the non-type-1 share.
papers.design: Serial cross-sectional analysis of hospital discharge data, joinpoint trend
papers.population_and_size: US National Inpatient Sample 2000-2014 (all ages, primary DKA code); denominators from NHIS
papers.measure_type: none (no insulin or C-peptide measurement in the paper)
papers.assay_or_platform: ICD-9-CM 250.1 administrative codes; no laboratory data
papers.quality_note: MMWR report by CDC authors; no ICD validation; event-level not patient-level; includes children; authors list euglycemic DKA and lower admission thresholds as possible reasons for the rise.

papers.relied_on: Row 32 D7 took 184,255 adult DKA events in 2014 (168,185 admissions plus 16,070 treated-and-released ED visits) and 70.6% type 1 to derive about 54,000 events not coded type 1.
papers.full_text_shows: The figures match Table 1 exactly (type 2 coded 53,941 of 184,255 in 2014; 799 unknown type, so 70.6% is of coded events). Authors state ICD-9 coding was not validated against records, data are events not patients (readmissions counted), duration of diabetes is unknown so new-onset versus established cannot be separated, and they found no evidence that ketosis-prone diabetes is increasing; they describe it as obese patients who often recover without further insulin.
papers.quote: In that same year, there were 168,185 adult admissions to inpatient settings in U.S. hospitals for DKA.
papers.role_in_work: Main source for the D7 event count and type split of row 32.
papers.design: Serial cross-sectional analysis of national ED and inpatient samples, 2006-2015
papers.population_and_size: US adults with diabetes; NEDS and NIS, about 20% stratified samples weighted to national estimates
papers.assay_or_platform: ICD-9-CM first-listed codes 250.1 and 250.2; type from fifth digit
papers.quality_note: Unvalidated coding, event-level data, no new-onset split; a type-2 code is not the same as ketosis-prone diabetes; the 20% new-onset and 35% ketosis-prone shares used in the V1 range are not in this paper (assumptions or other source).

papers.relied_on: Row 47 D7 used the 2-12% LADA share (excerpt only). The same text was not used for row 47 D3, which V1 scored 1 from the Japanese criteria and ADA 2026 only.
papers.full_text_shows: LADA is 2-12% of all patients with diabetes (lower in primary care; 7-14% in Northern Europe and China, lower in African American and Hispanic people). The panel explicitly recommends C-peptide measurement in islet autoantibody-positive patients, with concurrent glucose 80-180 mg/dL, fasting, random or postprandial, and says C-peptide should be repeated at treatment failure to identify progression to insulin deficiency. Panel cutoffs: <0.3 nmol/L multiple-insulin regimen, 0.3-0.7 nmol/L gray area, >0.7 nmol/L modified T2D algorithm. The text states there are no guidelines for LADA management.
papers.quote: The panel recommends measurement of serum (plasma) C-peptide levels as a proxy for insulin secretion in islet-cell related autoantibody–positive patients
papers.key_numbers: LADA 2-12% of diabetes; C-peptide <0.3, 0.3-0.7, >0.7 nmol/L tiers; follow-up at least every 6 months in the gray area
papers.role_in_work: D7 prevalence source for row 47; also an international consensus recommending C-peptide in the row 47 population (relevant to D3).
papers.design: Expert panel consensus statement (narrative review plus management proposal)
papers.population_and_size: Adults with LADA / autoantibody-positive slowly progressive diabetes; no patient data
papers.measure_type: C-peptide: fasting, random or postprandial (mixed-meal test called gold standard but not routine; 2-h post-meal value used by some laboratories)
papers.assay_or_platform: Not specified; said to be commercially available, inexpensive, widely accessible, not standardized for post-meal use
papers.quality_note: Consensus, not a guideline of a named society (endorsement by ADA or EASD not verified from the text); thresholds are panel proposals backed by two prospective studies; conflict-of-interest section not found in the stored text.

papers.relied_on: Row 47 entries treated fasting C-peptide <0.6 ng/mL as one of three required criteria for definite SPIDDM, a Japanese national expert criterion with no derivation, and (for D4) a standard single-sample test.
papers.full_text_shows: Confirmed: criterion 3 is insulin requirement for more than 3 months plus fasting serum C-peptide <0.6 ng/mL at the last observed time point; without it the case is 'probable'. The cutoff is stated to be the same as for acute-onset type 1 diabetes; no data derive it. The text names no C-peptide assay, no glucose condition and no timing; it excludes treatment from the criteria. It allows patients treated with insulin within 3 months by clinical judgment to meet criterion 3 if C-peptide is <0.6. Several authors report lecture fees or funding from Novo, Lilly, Sanofi, Terumo and others, and funding from Sysmex and Cosmic.
papers.quote: Notably, therapeutic intervention was not included in these new diagnostic criteria
papers.key_numbers: Fasting serum C-peptide <0.6 ng/mL; insulin more than 3 months (6 months typical); definite needs all 3 criteria, probable needs criteria 1 and 2
papers.role_in_work: Primary source for row 47 (national diagnostic criterion, Japan).
papers.design: Committee diagnostic criteria with short rationale (English version)
papers.population_and_size: Japanese adults and youth with islet autoantibody-positive diabetes; no patient numbers
papers.quality_note: Expert criteria, no evidence table; the 3-month insulin and C-peptide rule is borrowed from the acute-onset criteria.

papers.relied_on: Row 47 D2 and D8 used the 60-patient study as supporting data, noting that fasting C-peptide raised the PPV for progression but its contribution over insulin requirement was not tested.
papers.full_text_shows: Confirmed and refined. Of 60 patients, 30 were insulin dependent (F-CPR <0.6) within 3 years, including 7 already below 0.6 at entry. Baseline F-CPR <1.41 ng/mL added to high-titre GADA gave PPV 81.0% (RIA) and 79.0% (ELISA) against 70.0% and 73.1% for titre alone; age and BMI added about as much (76.9-84.2%), CIs overlap widely, NPV stayed 43-56%. These patients come from TIDE-J, the same registry as C306. The authors list small size, prior insulin use and prevalent cases as limitations.
papers.quote: factors beyond immunotype play a significant role in predicting progression to an ID state
papers.key_numbers: n=60; 30 progressed; PPV RIA-GADA 56.3% (any positive), 70.0% (>=10 U/mL), 81.0% with F-CPR <1.41 ng/mL; NPV 55.6%; F-CPR cutoff 1.41 ng/mL sens 90.0% spec 66.7%
papers.role_in_work: Prognostic evidence that baseline fasting C-peptide predicts later insulin dependence (F-CPR <0.6 is the outcome).
papers.design: Retrospective analysis within a multicentre prospective registry
papers.population_and_size: 60 Japanese adults with SPIDDM, mean age at diagnosis 53 years, diabetes duration 2.6 years
papers.measure_type: C-peptide (fasting) as predictor and as outcome; non-C-peptide markers: GADA by RIA and ELISA, IA-2A
papers.assay_or_platform: RSR RIA and ELISA kits for GADA; C-peptide assay not named in the stored text
papers.quality_note: Small, same measure defines outcome and predictor, no comparison with insulin requirement, funding disclosures include Cosmic (GADA ELISA maker) and Sysmex; not independent of C306.

papers.relied_on: Row 47 D2 cited TIDE-J (n=314; 9.1% of slowly progressive cases reached undetectable C-peptide by 5 years) as supporting data for the 0.6 ng/mL criterion.
papers.full_text_shows: The 9.1% (7 of the slowly progressive group) is undetectable C-peptide (<0.03 ng/mL), not the 0.6 ng/mL criterion. The endpoint that matches row 47, F-CPR <0.6 ng/mL, was reached by 41.3% at 5 years and 57.9% at 10 years (n=105 slowly progressive; 25 already definite at entry). In Cox models low BMI (HR 0.87) and GADA positivity (HR 11.69) predicted insulin dependence. Fasting C-peptide is the outcome, not a tested decision tool.
papers.quote: Insulin dependency was defined by F-CPR level <0.6 ng/mL
papers.key_numbers: n=314 (165 acute-onset, 105 slowly progressive, 44 fulminant); slowly progressive: undetectable CPR 9.1% at 5 y, 16.4% at 10 y; F-CPR <0.6 in 41.3% at 5 y, 57.9% at 10 y
papers.role_in_work: Natural-history cohort for the progression endpoint of row 47; background for the research use of C-peptide as a staging endpoint.
papers.design: Nationwide multicentre prospective longitudinal cohort, annual fasting C-peptide, up to 14 years
papers.population_and_size: 314 Japanese adults with type 1 diabetes, 105 slowly progressive
papers.measure_type: C-peptide (fasting, annual); HLA and autoantibodies as predictors
papers.assay_or_platform: Institution assays at entry (detection limit <0.01 or 0.02 ng/mL), central assay annually (<0.03 ng/mL); assay brand not named
papers.quality_note: Prospective, good follow-up design; mixed assays at entry; Japanese population, results may not transfer to US; overlaps with C285.

proposals.reason: V1 scored D3 on the Japanese national criteria and ADA 2026 only. The LADA international consensus (C063) recommends C-peptide measurement in autoantibody-positive patients for treatment choice and repeats it at treatment failure to identify progression to insulin deficiency. This covers the use-case population and the progression decision explicitly (clarification 14), so 3. Limits: expert panel statement that itself says there are no guidelines; endorsement by a named body not verified in the text; its tiers are in nmol/L (<0.3, 0.3-0.7), not the 0.6 ng/mL criterion; fasting, random or postprandial. If the reviewer reads a panel statement as short of 'guideline', 2 is the fallback.
proposals.quote: C-peptide measurement should drive the decision-making process for the choice of LADA treatment.

proposals.reason: C104 gives no derivation; C285 and C306 use F-CPR <0.6 as the outcome and are from the same registry (TIDE-J), so they are not independent and test no decision. 2 stays defensible (cohort data); 1 is arguable. The 9.1% figure in the reason should be replaced by 41.3% (5 y) and 57.9% (10 y) for F-CPR <0.6.
proposals.quote: Insulin dependency was defined by F-CPR level <0.6 ng/mL

proposals.reason: C285: F-CPR <1.41 ng/mL raised PPV only to 81.0/79.0%, similar to age or BMI, with overlapping CIs; no test against insulin requirement. Matches the current 2 (mechanism and one small study).
proposals.quote: factors beyond immunotype play a significant role in predicting progression to an ID state

proposals.reason: Not a change from C104 alone: C104 confirms the criterion is Japanese expert criteria. The change comes only from C063 (see the D3 proposal above).
proposals.quote: Notably, therapeutic intervention was not included in these new diagnostic criteria

proposals.reason: C104 confirms C-peptide <0.6 splits definite from probable SPIDDM (classification) under clarification 12; no treatment statement in the text. D4, D5, D6 and S: C104 names no assay, owner or burden, so it neither supports nor contradicts these.
proposals.quote: Notably, therapeutic intervention was not included in these new diagnostic criteria

proposals.reason: C063 confirms 2-12% LADA of all diabetes, lower in primary care and in African American and Hispanic people, which favours the lower part of the 5,000-70,000 range but stays inside bin 3 (point 20,000). The paper's denominator is all people with diabetes, not new adult diagnoses.
proposals.quote: account for 2–12% of all patients with diabetes

proposals.reason: C246 table figures match the reason exactly (184,255; 168,185; 16,070; 70.6%; about 54,000 not type 1). Coding is unvalidated and event-level and cannot split new-onset, so the 20% new-onset and 35% ketosis-prone shares remain assumptions. C230 gives 188,950 all-age hospitalizations, consistent. Range 13,000-80,000 stays in bin 3; the low end is close to the bin 2 boundary.

claim_issues.where: usecases/scoring/V1.json row 47 D7 reason (and any ledger line copying it)
claim_issues.issue: The reason says 2-12% of adult-onset diabetes; C063 says 2-12% of all patients with diabetes. The 10.2% African-American figure is from another source, and C063 says rates are lower in African American and Hispanic people than in Northern Europe and China (7-14%).
claim_issues.proposed_wording: LADA accounts for 2-12% of all patients with diabetes, with lower rates in primary care and in African American and Hispanic individuals (Buzzetti 2020, full text).

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 47 (Limited, Japanese national expert criteria) and merged-conclusion.md if it says no international source covers row 47
claim_issues.issue: The row cites only the Japanese criteria. C063 is an international consensus that recommends C-peptide in autoantibody-positive LADA patients (tiers <0.3, 0.3-0.7, >0.7 nmol/L; repeat at treatment failure). Row 6 already cites C063 for LADA; row 47 should link to it. Status 'limited' may stay because it is a panel statement and not a guideline.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Add: International LADA expert panel (Buzzetti 2020, PMID 32847960, DOI 10.2337/dbi20-0017, full text) recommends C-peptide measurement in autoantibody-positive patients and repeat measurement at treatment failure to identify progression to insulin deficiency; thresholds differ from the Japanese 0.6 ng/mL criterion.

claim_issues.issue: '9.1 percent reached undetectable C-peptide by 5 years' is a different endpoint from the 0.6 ng/mL criterion. TIDE-J (C306) and the 60-patient study (C285) overlap and are not independent.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: In TIDE-J (n=105 slowly progressive), fasting C-peptide <0.6 ng/mL was reached by 41.3% at 5 years and 57.9% at 10 years; undetectable C-peptide (<0.03 ng/mL) by 9.1% and 16.4%. The 60-patient study is drawn from the same registry.

claim_issues.issue: 'PPV from about 56-72 to 77-84 percent' blends several steps; fasting C-peptide specifically gave 81.0% (RIA) and 79.0% (ELISA) versus 70.0% and 73.1% for high-titre GADA alone, similar to age or BMI.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Adding fasting C-peptide <1.41 ng/mL to high-titre GADA raised PPV from 70.0 to 81.0% (RIA) and from 73.1 to 79.0% (ELISA), about the same as age or BMI; NPV 43-56%; n=60.

notes: All six texts read from corpus/fulltext (good quality, tables intact; non-breaking hyphens in C285 and C104). Current scores read from V1 to V5; I did not find a later correction or supersede for the cited row 32 D7 or row 47 entries (I checked only the V1-V5 files for these dimensions; the correction on row 32 V5 S does not concern them). Path to viability for row 47 is affected: C063 gives an international consensus route, so harmonising cutoffs and assays is the step (the Japanese 0.6 ng/mL is roughly 0.2 nmol/L [recall, my conversion] and differs from the panel 0.3 nmol/L tier). Row 32 path unaffected. Conflicts of interest for C063 not found in the stored text. Tool calls used: about 12 including the two file writes (one shell call failed on a quoting error and was repeated with the Write tool).
